data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Reliability gains are genuine only if the panel identifies 'hidden' failure modes that the checklist did not explicitly prompt for, but which were uncovered by the diversity of non-expert perspectives.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel members are incentivized to avoid conflict and simply 'check the box'.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is so exhaustive that no external observations are possible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Genuine reliability gain is distinguished from mere compliance by the presence of 'emergent corrections'\u2014instances where a panel member flags a discrepancy between the checklist's literal requirement and the actual state of the object, leading to a correct judgment that a rigid application of the checklist would have missed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
